name: Fuladl

facts.text: Level 77, 30,000 health. Spawns four or five smaller 'Part of Fuladl' when fought.
Ful 'foul' and adl 'disease, sickness' are standard glosses; the reading 'foul sickness' is to verify.

story:
Not everything in Krondon came up with the ogres. Some of it was always there, waiting in the low places where the old hall's drains ran. Fuladl is one of those: a rot that learned to move. The hall's last keepers named it as they named everything, with a plain word for a plain horror, the foul sickness. Cut it and it comes apart into smaller pieces of itself that crawl back toward you. The ogres will not go near it. They feed it what they do not want, and that is how they keep their hall clean, and that is why it has grown so large.

What the hall-folk walled away. Not everything in Krondon came up with the ogres. Some of it was always there, in the low places where the old hall's drains ran down to the sea. The hall-folk knew it. When the rot in the drains began to move, they walled the drains up and wrote its name over the bricks in the plainest words they had: Fuladl, the foul sickness. They meant it as a warning to their children. Their children are ghosts now, and the ogres cannot read.

Why it splits. The ogres broke the wall for the space behind it, and Fuladl came out, and it has been growing ever since on everything the ogres throw down the drains. It has no mind, only appetite, and it does not die cleanly: cut it and it comes apart into four or five smaller pieces of itself that crawl back toward whoever is warmest. The ogres will not go near it. They feed it what they do not want, and that is how they keep their hall clean, and that is why it has grown so large.
legend:
Cut Fuladl and pieces of him split off. Kill the pieces fast or you are fighting five of him, and the healers will be the first thing they find. Fulafeallan in the next passage does the same; do not pull both, and do not chase a piece into the dark.

Pieces go for whoever is warmest, which means the healers. Keep an area-damage caster on the pieces and nothing else, and never fight it in the narrow drain mouth where the pieces cannot be reached. The old hands bring torches and a cleric with a strong stomach, and say the smell is the hardest part of the fight. They are joking, mostly. The pieces are slow; the casters should never be caught by them.

loremasterTopic.text: A rot that learned to move, down in the hall's old drains. The keepers called it the foul sickness. Cut it and it comes apart; kill the pieces before they come back together around you.

bookPage: Below the hall run the drains the hall-folk walled up, and over the bricks they wrote the name of what lived there in plain words for a plain horror: the foul sickness. The ogres broke the wall for the space. When we went down, the thing filled the passage from side to side and moved toward our torches. We cut it, and it came apart, and the pieces crawled toward our priests as if they knew which of us kept the others alive. We burned them one by one. The smell has not left my cloak.
